nodes.name: Electrodeposition of 2D Co(OH)2
nodes.procedure: A three-electrode system, which consisted of a piece of carbon clothes as the working electrode, a platinum plate as a counter electrode, and a saturated calomel electrode (SCE) as a reference electrode, was used for electrodeposition. Before electrodeposition, a Co(NO3)2 solution (30 mM) was prepared as the electrolyte. The electrodeposition experiments were conducted at a constant potential of -1.0 V versus SCE for 300 s. After deposition, the obtained 2D cobalt hydroxides nanosheets arrays (denoted 2D Co(OH)2) was washed with deionized water and ethanol for several times, and then dried at 60 °C for 6 h.
nodes.source_text: Synthesis of 2D Co(OH)2: According to previous literatures, a facile electrodeposition method was employed to prepare 2D cobalt hydroxides nanosheets arrays supported on the carbon clothes... dried at 60 °C for 6 h.

nodes.name: Hydrothermal transformation to hierarchical Co-PBAs
nodes.procedure: K3[Co(CN)6] (0.3 mmol) was dissolved in 30 mL deionized water to prepare a clear solution of A. Then, the solution A and a piece of carbon cloth containing the above synthesized 2D Co(OH)2 were transferred into a 50 mL Teflon-lined autoclave, which was then heated to 60 °C for 4 h using an electric oven. After the autoclave cooled down to room temperature, the piece of carbon cloth was washed using deionized water and ethanol for several times, and dried in vacuum oven at 60 °C for 6 h. At this moment, the 2D Co(OH)2 was transformed into 3D Co-based Prussian blue analogue (Co-PBAs) cubes interconnected on the 2D Co-PBAs nanosheet arrays (denoted hierarchical Co-PBAs nanocubes).
nodes.source_text: Synthesis of Hierarchical CoS2 Nanocages: K3[Co(CN)6] (0.3 mmol) was dissolved in 30 mL deionized water... dried in vacuum oven at 60 °C for 6 h.

nodes.name: S2- etching to hierarchical CoS2 nanocages
nodes.procedure: The hierarchical Co-PBAs nanocubes were etched by S2- anions using a Na2S solution at 60 °C for 6 h. The Na2S solution was prepared by dissolving Na2S·9H2O (60 mg) in a mixed solution (30 mL) of ethanol and deionized water with a volume ratio of 2:1 (ethanol:water).
nodes.source_text: Finally, the hierarchical Co-PBAs nanocubes were etched by S2- anions using a Na2S solution at 60 °C for 6 h. The Na2S solution was prepared by dissolving Na2S·9H2O (60 mg) in a mixed solution (30 mL) of ethanol and deionized water with a volume ratio of 2:1.

nodes.name: Calcination for partial S edge removal
nodes.procedure: To remove the S edges of CoS2, the hierarchical CoS2 nanocages were calcinated at 300 °C for 1 h under the atmosphere of Ar, and the calcinated product was denoted hierarchical CoS2 nanocages-300.
nodes.source_text: To remove the S edges of CoS2, the hierarchical CoS2 nanocages were calcinated at 300 °C for 1 h under the atmosphere of Ar...

nodes.source_text: Though they have the similar reduction current density, the hierarchical CoS2 nanocages enabled much smaller Faradic efficiencies toward carbon monoxide (CO) (FE_CO) but larger Faradic efficiencies toward hydrogen (FE_H2) than that of hierarchical CoS2 nanocages-300 over the whole potential windows (Figure 3b, and Figure S9, Supporting Information). For example, ... at the same potential, the hierarchical CoS2 nanocages displayed a small FE_CO of 42.4% and large FE_H2 of 57%

nodes.description: CO2RR performance in CO2-saturated 0.5 M KHCO3
nodes.source_text: As displayed in Figure 3a, the hierarchical CoS2 nanocages-300 possessed high activity for CO2RR with the onset overpotential of −0.2 V versus RHE... the hierarchical CoS2 nanocages-300 achieved the maximum FE_CO of 85.7% at a potential of −0.6 V versus RHE along with FE_H2 of 13.5%... partial CO current density (jCO) of 2.8 mA cm−2... the hierarchical CoS2 nanocages-300 possessed Cdl of 8.0 mF... excellent stability for CO2RR without obvious deactivation at seven different potentials from −0.2 to −0.8 V during 2000-s continuous CO2RR

nodes.characterization_summary: No XRD peaks for CoS2 observed due to low mass loading or poor crystallinity of hierarchical CoS2 nanocages.
nodes.evidence_snippet: However, no XRD peaks corresponding to Co sulfides were evidenced on the hierarchical CoS2 nanocages due to low mass loading (merely 0.5 mg cm^-2) or poor crystallinity of generated Co sulfides.

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM shows well-retained 2D nanosheet arrays with contorted edges of nanocages indicating reaction between S^2- and Co-PBAs.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In case of hierarchical CoS2 nanocages... the nanostructure of 2D nanosheet arrays was well retained but the edges of nanocages became contorted (Figure 2a), indicating the presence of reaction between S^2- and Co-PBAs.

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM confirms transformation of solid Co-PBAs nanocubes to hollow-structured CoS2 nanocages.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The morphology of hierarchical CoS2 nanocages were further investigated by transmission electron microscopy (TEM) (Figure 2b,c), signifying that the solid Co-PBAs nanocubes were transformed to hollow-structured CoS2 nanocages by S^2- etching.

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM reveals lattice fringes spaced 0.27 nm corresponding to (200) plane of CoS2; hierarchical CoS2 nanocages-300 shows distorted lattice fringes at marginal areas due to S edge removal.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Corresponding high-resolution TEM (HRTEM) images revealed the presence of clear lattice fringes in spacing of 0.27 nm (Figure 2d), which can be attributed to (200) plane of CoS2.

nodes.characterization_summary: Atomic ratio of Co/S is nearly 2, confirming formation of CoS2.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The result characterized by inductively coupled plasma-atomic emission spectrometry (ICP-AES) indicated that the atomic ration of Co/S was nearly 2, further confirming the formation of CoS2.

nodes.characterization_summary: TGA shows first mass loss of 25 wt% at 30-300°C attributed to adsorbed water, S edges, and part of plane S; second mass loss of 38 wt% at 300-750°C.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As displayed in Figure 2a, there are two mass loss during the calcination of hierarchical CoS2 nanocages: the first mass loss of 25 wt% at the temperature range of 30-300°C... and the second mass loss of 38 wt% at the temperature of 300-750°C.

nodes.characterization_summary: Raman shows sharp peak at 678 cm^-1 for S-S bonds and peaks at 186, 468, 513 cm^-1 for Co-S bonds; peaks weaken after calcination at 300°C indicating partial S removal.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Raman spectra of hierarchical CoS2 nanocages displayed a sharp peak at 678 cm^-1 for S−S bonds and other small peaks for Co−S bands (i.e., 186, 468, and 513 cm^-1)... Upon calcination at 300°C... the Raman peak for both S−S and Co−S bonds were weakened.

nodes.characterization_summary: S 2p XPS shows peaks at 162.0 eV (S 2p3/2, edges) and 163.3 eV (S 2p1/2, plane S); ratio of S^2- edges/plane S^2- is ≈1.01 for hierarchical CoS2 nanocages and ≈0.28 for -300 sample.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The S 2p XPS spectra of hierarchical CoS2 nanocages and Hierarchical CoS2 nanocages-300 showed two peaks at 162.0 and 163.3 eV corresponding to S 2p3/2 and S 2p1/2... the ratio of S^2- edges/plane S^2- in the hierarchical CoS2 nanocages was calculated to be ≈1.01, much higher than that of hierarchical CoS2 nanocages-300 (≈0.28).

nodes.characterization_summary: Double-layer capacitance Cdl = 8.0 mF for hierarchical CoS2 nanocages-300, indicating higher ECSA than powder CoS2 nanocages-300.
nodes.evidence_snippet: It was found that the hierarchical CoS2 nanocages-300 possessed Cdl of 8.0 mF, 2.4-fold larger than that of CoS2 nanocages-300, reflecting that the hierarchical CoS2 nanocages-300 could provide more active sites for electrocatalysis.
